chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ma'alla ibn Khunays, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Should I buy the crop?' He said, 'When it is the size of a span.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for selling crops before harvest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in agricultural sales by setting a tangible threshold for crop maturity. The 'size of a span' (*qadr shibr*) serves as a practical metric to ensure the crop is sufficiently established and visible, thereby validating the transaction before harvest. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing ambiguity in commercial contracts by anchoring validity to observable physical states.
